messages:
maria: FYI Acme reported a sharp jump in cross-region token usage and unexpected duplicate billing. They say ~20-30% of requests that should be routed to eu-west are landing in us-east and sometimes both.
ryan: customer provided sample request IDs and timestamps, attached in the ticket. billing shows two charges for single calls in a short window. :frowning:
sam: can you paste the SDK config they used? hedging/backoff settings are my first suspect.
maria: here's their config snippet they pasted:
```json
{
  "endpoint": "api.redwood.ai",
  "region_preference": "eu-west",
  "hedged_requests": true,
  "hedged_timeout_ms": 120,
  "request_timeout_ms": 500,
  "backoff": { "base_ms": 50, "max_ms": 2000 }
}
```
jonathan: aha. hedged_timeout_ms at 120ms is pretty aggressive for inter-region variance and DNS/route differences. If the client fires a hedged request to fallback region before the initial completes we can see double counting (both accepted) and cross-region latency.
sam: do our servers dedupe by client-request-id? We only have idempotency for non-streaming endpoints. Generation calls are charged per token; if both requests reach different model pools they both get billed.
jonathan: correct. No automatic server-side dedupe for generation. We log X-Request-Route and X-Instance-ID; can we map the sample request IDs to those headers?
maria: yes, attached logs show for request 7f3a: first hit eu-west-2 node, second hit us-east-1 node within 150ms.
ryan: customer says they didn't intentionally enable cross-region fallback; they relied on region_preference.
sam: region_preference doesn't prevent hedging fallback. Hedged requests are sent to a secondary route according to the client's routing policy when the hedged timeout triggers. If the fallback route is in another region, you'll get hops.
maria: what's the immediate mitigation we can recommend so they stop getting double charges?
jonathan: tell them to disable hedged_requests or raise hedged_timeout_ms to something closer to 250-400ms, and set backoff base to larger value. Also recommend setting prefer_local_route: true (client-side) to avoid fallback going cross-region.
sam: I'll draft a quick patch note + sample config. Proposed quickfix:
```json
{
  "hedged_requests": false,
  "request_timeout_ms": 800,
  "prefer_local_route": true
}
```
maria: customer applied disable hedging and reported no duplicates for 2 hours, but latency spikes for some requests remain.
jonathan: those spikes could be real performance regressions in eu-west; hedging was masking them by hitting us-east. We should surface per-route latency percentiles in the console so customers can choose.
sam: opened an internal ticket to add: 1) server-side metric to flag dual-accept (two accepted responses same client request id range), 2) UX banner suggesting hedging best practices by region. ticket: TKT-5123
deploy-bot: canary rollout for hedging-docs update scheduled for 2050003200 by @sam.
ryan: customer wants a credit for the duplicated charges. finance policy?
maria: support can submit a billing dispute, point to the disabled hedging as mitigation. I'll escalate to billing after we confirm there were two accepted charges.
jonathan: long-term fix: we should add a client-side routing knob to prefer-same-region-failover-only (i.e., fall back within region or availability zone before cross-region). Also consider server-side sequence numbers to dedupe accepted generation requests when duplicate payloads arrive within short windows.
sam: agreed. I'll add design notes to the ticket. For now, update the KB article: "Avoid unintended cross-region hedging" and include sample configs and recommended defaults.
maria: thanks team — I'll update the customer and file the billing dispute. :thumbsup:
ryan: thanks, folks.
